title: Question 14744
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Lydia was the manager of a privately owned Christian bookstore. She was fired and told to leave the building immediately. Lydia went home, but she returned that night to retrieve personal study notes from her office. When she discovered that her key no longer opened the rear door, she forced the door open and went to her former office. To avoid attracting attention, she did not turn on any lights. In the dark, she knew that she was putting some items into her bag that were not hers; she planned to sort them out later and return them. At home, Lydia found that she had taken the store’s order ledger and several vendor invoices. After thinking it over and becoming angrier about being fired, she burned the ledger and invoices in her fireplace.

The jurisdiction has expanded the crime of burglary to include all buildings.

What crime(s) has Lydia committed?
rightExplanation:
C is correct.

Silver Key: When the choices are “both / burglary only / larceny only / neither,” do not treat the four answers as four independent rules. Resolve the two crime clocks separately, then combine them.

Gold Key: Burglary turns on the intent at entry. Lydia forced the door open, but she entered to retrieve her own study notes. The later decision to take or destroy the bookstore’s property does not backfill the burglary intent at the time of entry.

Gold Key: Larceny can attach through continuing trespass. Lydia knowingly carried away property that was not hers, planned to return it, and later formed the intent to permanently deprive by burning it. That makes larceny, but not burglary.

c3.label: Array read
c3.text:
A = burglary yes / larceny yes.
B = burglary yes / larceny no.
C = burglary no / larceny yes.
D = burglary no / larceny no.

c3.label: CUT
c3.text: no pure structural cut. This is anchor-dependent. The answer choices are a clean 2×2 matrix.

c3.label: CLASH axis 1 — burglary
c3.text:
Did Lydia have the crime intent at entry?
Splitting fact: she returned to retrieve her own study notes.
Result: no burglary.

c3.label: CLASH axis 2 — larceny
c3.text:
Did the later decision to destroy the property matter?
Splitting fact: she knowingly carried away property not hers, then burned it before returning it.
Result: larceny.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: combine the two axes. No burglary + larceny = C.

studentScript: This is a two-crime matrix. Burglary clock: at entry she was retrieving her own notes, so no burglary. Larceny clock: she knowingly took store property and later burned it, so larceny. Answer C.

A.signal: A is the dominant trap because it combines the true larceny axis with the false burglary axis.
A.lawyer: No burglary because the required intent was absent at entry; larceny remains through continuing trespass.

B.signal: B treats later intent as enough for burglary and later destruction as irrelevant to larceny.
B.lawyer: Later intent does not backfill burglary, but later permanent-deprivation intent can complete larceny under continuing trespass.

C.signal: C is the only answer matching both resolved axes.
C.lawyer: Matches the official rule: larceny through continuing trespass; no burglary without entry-time felonious intent.

D.signal: D notices the no-burglary fact but misses the later larceny fact.
D.lawyer: Initial plan to return does not defeat larceny once the later intent to destroy forms during the continuing trespass.

goldKeys.statement: Burglary requires the intent to commit the target crime at entry. Later-formed intent inside the building does not backfill burglary.
goldKeys.trigger: Entry begins for one stated purpose; later bad intent appears only after entry.
goldKeys.authority: Common-law burglary: breaking and entering with intent to commit felony; prompt modifies building scope only.

goldKeys.statement: If the taking is trespassory, the trespass can continue; a later intent to keep or destroy before return can supply larceny intent.
goldKeys.trigger: Takes property not hers intending to return, then later keeps or destroys it.

silverKeys.statement: For both/burglary-only/larceny-only/neither choices, solve each crime as a separate yes/no axis, then combine.
silverKeys.trigger: Answer choices list every combination of two crimes.

remediation.title: Two intent clocks: entry clock and taking clock
remediation.signal: Crime-combination answer array with burglary and larceny.
remediation.studentMove: Resolve burglary at entry; resolve larceny across the taking/return timeline.
remediation.tinyRule: Entry intent controls burglary; continuing trespass can let later steal intent complete larceny.
remediation.trap: Forced entry plus later destruction tempts students to say both crimes.
